subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw add diagnostics-only declared/effective tool visibility first, or also add a default-off strict inheritance mode that fails sessions when declared and effective tools diverge?
rationale: The choice changes the authority boundary between agent config and lower runtime/session security layers and adds public config/protocol surface.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured clipping reasons while keeping lower runtime clipping authoritative.

options.title: Default-Off Strict Parity
options.body: Add an explicit strict option that fails closed on divergence with reporting, docs, and fresh-install plus upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Current Clipping
options.body: Keep the existing runtime-clipping model and document that declared config is not the final authority.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured clipping reasons while keeping lower runtime clipping authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent capability-profile work makes this the closest current owner for the security and product boundary decision.
